title: Kasparov vs Topalov, 1999 - Kasparov's Immortal
event: Hoogovens Tournament, Wijk aan Zee, Netherlands
notes: Sample game for testing the replay. The 'thoughts' are short notes written by hand (or plain move descriptions), not real AI thinking.

moves.thought: I claim the centre with my king's pawn.
A flexible setup. I will put my bishop on g7 later.
Queen and bishop line up to swap off Black's best bishop.
Offer to trade bishops so Black's king loses its guard.
I castle queenside and get my king to safety.
I castle queenside too. Both kings are now on the same side.
Check! Black's king has to step into the corner.
A rook sacrifice! If Black takes it, the king gets dragged into the open.
I'll take the free rook and see if the attack really works.
Check. The black king has nowhere safe to hide.
Queen takes Pawn on d4. Check!
Another check, pulling the king even further up the board.
I win a knight while the king is stuck on my side of the board.
Queen takes Pawn on a6. Check!
A quiet move with a sharp idea: my bishop now attacks Black's queen.
Black can no longer stop my passed pawns and threats. Black resigns.
